findings.title: Restart path no longer kills hung spawn-context flusher processes
findings.body: The restart path only calls `process.kill()` when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. Processes created via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process` are `SpawnProcess` instances, which derive from `BaseProcess` and are not subclasses of `multiprocessing.Process`. So the check is False in production and the old process is never killed. The pre-change code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally (catching only ValueError), so this is a regression. Consequence: when a flusher is detected as hung (stale `healthy_since`), it keeps running while a replacement is started on the same shards. If the old process recovers, two flushers run concurrently against the same Redis shards, which can produce duplicate or fragmented segments to buffered-segments. Each restart also leaks a live process. Fix by killing any process that supports kill (e.g. check against `multiprocessing.context.BaseProcess`), and add a test that exercises the restart path.

findings.title: join() never terminates spawn-context flusher processes
findings.body: The `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` check is False for `SpawnProcess` objects (the type returned by the spawn context used at line 53), so `process.terminate()` is never called in `join()`. The loop was rewritten in this PR, but the check is still wrong. If a flusher is still alive after the join timeout, it is left running until the parent exits. The check should use `BaseProcess` or a duck-typed check.

findings.title: Unused `_create_process_for_shard` would orphan a live process if called
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard` is added but never called in this PR. If it is called, it invokes `_create_process_for_shards`, which starts a new process and overwrites `self.processes[process_index]` without killing or joining the existing process. The old process is then unreferenced and keeps flushing its shards. Either remove the dead method or make it kill the existing process first.

findings.title: The added `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op, so the test is still racy
findings.body: The test patches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None` at line 15 via monkeypatch. The `time.sleep(0.1)` added here therefore does nothing, despite the comment saying it gives flusher threads time to run. `step.join()` then sets `stopped` while the flusher thread may not yet have called `flush_segments` after the drift change. The `(msg,) = messages` assertion can then fail intermittently. The wait should be a real deadline loop that polls `messages`, or the sleep reference should be captured before patching.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag keys: "shards" vs "shard" with comma-joined values
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses the tag key "shards" (line 199), while `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` (line 185), `segment_size_bytes` (line 195), and `flusher_unhealthy` (line 244) use "shard". For multi-shard processes, the "shard" value is a comma-joined list, while `flusher_unhealthy` uses a single integer shard id under the same key. Dashboards and alerts that group by `shard` will not line up across these metrics, and the `wait_produce` series changes identity from untagged to tagged. Use one tag key and one value format across all flusher metrics.

findings.title: Docstring says one process per shard, but the default is a single process
findings.body: The class docstring says the flusher "Creates one process per shard". The code actually creates `min(max_processes, len(shards))` processes, and the consumer's `--flusher-processes` option defaults to 1. With default settings, all shards are handled by one process. The docstring and the help text should say this accurately.

findings.title: Unrelated guideline added to a span flusher PR
findings.body: The new "Use hasattr() for unions" anti-pattern section has nothing to do with the multiprocessed span flusher change. It should be split into its own PR so the change history stays reviewable and the guidance can be discussed separately.
